messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: k-privnet (Kestrel Enterprise) experiencing elevated 503s from their private pool. Source: NLB -> backend rejects. Alert rate spiked 2026-06-05T14:12Z. Pager routed to oncall.

alice (oncall): seeing the same in console, 503s for /v1/generate from Kestrel tenant. NLB healthchecks still show healthy.

raj (network): can you paste a sample 503 log? NLB passthrough suggests backend reset or security group drop.

alice (oncall): here's a snippet: 
```
2026-06-05T14:11:59Z backend1 10.0.40.12:5040 -> RST
2026-06-05T14:12:02Z client 10.1.12.5 -> 503
```

marta (solutions): customer (kestrel-support) says they rolled out a managed SG sync earlier today to tighten source CIDR for app-to-app. Might be related.

kestrel-support: confirmed — we pushed a whitelist update at 13:58 UTC that narrowed allowed agent CIDRs. We did not change NLB healthcheck source CIDR.

bryan (sre-lead): two hypotheses: 1) backend processes rejecting connection due to client IP mapping change (X-Forwarded-For) 2) SG is dropping ephemeral probe connections from internal probe addresses. Check conntrack / dropped packets.

raj (network): running quick tcpdump on host (outbound to backend) and checking SG flow logs.

ops-bot: flow-log sample (recent): 
```
ALLOW 10.3.0.0/16 -> 10.0.40.12:5040 tcp SYN (ACCEPT)
DROP 172.31.0.0/16 -> 10.0.40.12:5040 tcp SYN (DROP) rule-id: 902
```

alice (oncall): looks like some health probes originate from 172.31.x.x (internal probe pool). Kestrel SG tightened to 10.3.0.0/16 only; probes now blocked -> backend returns connection resets -> NLB treats as unhealthy intermittently -> client sees 503s.

marta (solutions): customer, can you temporarily widen the SG to include the probe CIDR (172.31.0.0/16) or add a short-lived rule?

kestrel-support: we can add a temporary rule for probe CIDRs for 30m. Doing it now. Patch ID: kestrel-sg-20260605-temp.

raj (network): verifying flow logs after rule change...

ops-bot: flow-log sample (post-change): 
```
ALLOW 172.31.0.0/16 -> 10.0.40.12:5040 tcp SYN (ACCEPT) rule-id: kestrel-sg-20260605-temp
```

alice (oncall): service error rate dropping back to baseline. 503s down from 12/min to 0-1/min. Confirming with Kestrel. :thumbsup:

kestrel-support: client error rate normalizing. Thanks, that fixed it.

bryan (sre-lead): good short-term fix. Next: need a durable solution — either pin healthcheck source CIDR to allowed list or ensure managed SG sync excludes probe CIDRs.

marta (solutions): action items for post-incident: 1) add preflight check in our onboarding docs for customers that apply SG syncs (detect accidentally blocking internal probe ranges), 2) create automation that warns when a SG change would drop probe CIDRs.

raj (network): I'll open a ticket to add a periodic audit that compares customer SGs against our probe/worker CIDRs and flag risky changes.

alice (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: watch Kestrel err rate and watch for repeated SG syncs; if error persists, escalate to dedicated pool failover.

ops-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 2026-06-05T14:23Z. Root cause provisional: customer SG whitelist update blocked internal probe CIDR, causing intermittent backend connection resets and NLB-level 503s.

bryan (sre-lead): will schedule a short postmortem with Kestrel and Solutions next week. Assigning follow-ups: SRE-847 (audit job), SOL-319 (onboarding docs), NETWORK-612 (probe CIDR pinning).

alice (oncall): thanks all, handing off to night oncall.
